outcome: Incidence of short cervical length (≤25 mm) in the second trimester
cohort: Women with singleton gestations without prior spontaneous preterm birth undergoing universal second trimester transvaginal ultrasound cervical length screening between January 2012 and December 2013
finding: Black women had a 2.8-fold increased risk of short cervical length (≤25 mm) compared to non-Hispanic white women in a low-risk population.
mod_finding: This study found that Black women had higher rates of spontaneous preterm birth and were more likely to have their infants admitted to the NICU compared to non-Hispanic white women.
